119: ## 3. Local Streaming & Cryptographic Proxy Packaging
120: 
121: ### 3.1 Platform Constraint Analysis
122: 
123: Why does Cinejoy TV require a local streaming proxy?
124: 1. **Lightspeed CDN Origin Enforcement**: `https://lightspeed.st/hls/*` rejects any request lacking `Origin: https://cinejoy.pk` and `Referer: https://cinejoy.pk/` with **HTTP 404 Not Found**.
125: 2. **Browser Sandbox Header Prohibition**: Per the W3C Fetch / XMLHttpRequest specifications, the `Origin` and `Referer` headers are forbidden request headers. Chromium (~108+) on webOS strictly forbids client-side JavaScript or `<video>` elements from overriding `Origin` on outgoing requests.
126: 3. **Web Crypto & WASM in Browser vs Node.js**: While the browser runtime can execute `crush.wasm` and AES-256-GCM, it cannot serve or rewrite fragmented MP4 streams to `<video>` with the required spoofed origin headers. Hence, a Node.js proxy is technically mandatory.
127: 
128: ### 3.2 Evaluation of Three Packaging Topologies
129: 
130: | Dimension | Topology A: webOS JS Service | Topology B: Bundled in Web App | Topology C: Local Sidecar Daemon |
131: |---|---|---|---|
132: | **Structure** | `services/com.cinejoy.tv.service/` inside `.ipk` | Packaged inside `data/usr/palm/applications/` | Running external to webOS on TV or LAN |
133: | **Node.js Environment** | Native webOS Node.js process managed by SAM | Pure browser context (No Node.js available) | Host or local device Node.js runtime |
134: | **Origin Spoofing** | Supported (Node.js `http`/`https` built-ins) | **Impossible** (Chromium blocks header rewrite)| Supported |
135: | **TV Deployment Mode** | Fully self-contained in single `.ipk` | Non-viable (cannot stream video) | Requires separate SSH background process |
136: | **Verdict** | **Recommended for Production IPK** | **Incompatible** | **Recommended for Dev & Test Suites** |

178: #### Dual-Mode Execution in `index.js`:
179: On webOS, services are started by the webOS Luna Bus (`hub4it`) when an LS2 message arrives. In local testing or emulator mode, it is started via `node server/index.js`.

190:     message.respond({ returnValue: true, status: 'ok', port: activePort });

205: When the web application boots, it verifies proxy availability:
206: 1. Pings `http://127.0.0.1:8088/health`.
207: 2. If unreachable (e.g., TV just powered on and service is dormant), it issues a Luna bus wakeup:
208:    ```javascript
209:    if (window.webOS && window.webOS.service) {
210:      window.webOS.service.request('luna://com.cinejoy.tv.service', {
211:        method: 'ping',
212:        parameters: {},
213:        onSuccess: () => console.log('Proxy service awakened'),
214:        onFailure: (err) => console.warn('Luna ping failed, will retry HTTP', err)

430: Source-level inspection of `@webos-tools/cli/lib/package.js` (lines 1096–1127) reveals how `--app-exclude` / `-e` patterns are processed:
431: 
432: ```javascript
433: const regExpQueries = excludes.map(function(exclude) {
434:     return exclude.replace(/^\./g, "^\\.").replace(/^\*/g, "").replace(/$/g, "$");
435: });

438: Crucial implications:
439: 1. `ares-package` treats exclusion strings as raw regular expressions, appending a trailing `$` (end-of-string).
440: 2. If `-e "tests"` is passed, it generates `tests$`. It only matches when a directory path ends exactly with `tests`, but will NOT match child files like `tests/test1.js`.

443:    - `-e "*test.*"` transforms into `test.*$` (matches `test-m3.js`, `test-ui.js`, `test-m4-stress.js`).
444:    - `-e "*stress.*"` transforms into `stress.*$`.
445:    - `-e "*adversarial.*"` transforms into `adversarial.*$`.
446:    - `-e "*tests"` transforms into `tests$` (matches the tests directory).
447:    - `-e "*node_modules"` transforms into `node_modules$`.

12: ## 1. Executive Summary & Architecture Overview
13: 
14: The Cinejoy webOS TV application is engineered for the **LG 32LR686BPSA** television. It provides a 10-foot living-room cinema experience running at native **1920×1080 (1080p Full HD)** with a 60 FPS rendering target, deterministic spatial D-pad remote navigation, and hardware-accelerated HLS/fMP4 video playback.
15: 
16: Because the underlying video delivery network (`lightspeed.st`) enforces strict server-side origin policies (`Origin: https://cinejoy.pk` and `Referer: https://cinejoy.pk/`), the application utilizes a hybrid architecture:

18: 2. **Local Streaming & Cryptographic Proxy (`/server`)**: A lightweight Node.js daemon executing the `crush.wasm` + AES-256-GCM `lumen-gate-v2` stream resolver and transparently proxying HLS manifests and fMP4 segments with required headers.
19: 3. **Deployment Pipeline**: Packaged as a standard webOS `.ipk` archive via `@webos-tools/cli` and deployed over local network SSH (`port 9922`) to the LG Developer Mode sandbox (`prisoner` user).

47: ## 2. Target Hardware & Runtime Specifics
48: 
49: ### 2.1 Hardware Profile: LG 32LR686BPSA
50: - **Display Panel**: 32-inch Direct LED LCD, 16:9 aspect ratio, 60 Hz refresh rate.
51: - **Native Resolution**: **1920 × 1080 pixels** (Full HD).
52: - **SoC Architecture**: Quad-core ARM Cortex-A53/A55 processor (~1.1–1.3 GHz) with Mali/PowerVR GPU.
53: - **Total Physical RAM**: **1.5 GB system memory**.
54:   - Memory is shared globally across the Linux kernel, graphics framebuffers, Wayland/Ozone compositor, system services (Luna Bus), audio/video hardware pipelines, broadcast tuner buffers, and active apps.
55: - **Network Interfaces**:
56:   - Wi-Fi 5 (802.11ac, 2.4 GHz / 5 GHz dual-band).
57:   - 100 Mbps Fast Ethernet (RJ-45).

59: ### 2.2 webOS Platform & Runtime Environment
60: - **Operating System**: **LG webOS 8.5.0** (marketed under webOS 23 / webOS 24).
61: - **Firmware Version**: **13.50.44** (or latest OTA release).
62: - **Web Runtime**: **Chromium ~108+ embedded engine** managed by webOS WebAppManager (`WAM`).
63: - **Feature Support Matrix**:
64:   - WebAssembly (WASM): **Native support** (`WebAssembly.instantiate`). Used for `crush.wasm`.
65:   - Web Crypto API: **Native support** (`crypto.subtle.importKey`, `crypto.subtle.decrypt` for AES-256-GCM).
66:   - MediaSource Extensions (MSE): **Native support** for fragmented MP4 (ISO BMFF) via `hls.js`.
67:   - Video Codecs (Hardware Accelerated):
68:     - H.264 / AVC: High Profile Level 4.2 up to 1080p@60fps.
69:     - HEVC / H.265: Main / Main 10 Profile up to 1080p/2160p@60fps.
70:     - VP9: Profile 0/2 up to 1080p@60fps.

72:     - AAC-LC, HE-AAC v1/v2 (Stereo and 5.1).
73:     - Dolby Digital (AC-3) and Dolby Digital Plus (E-AC-3) pass-through / decode.
74:     - Linear PCM.

76: ### 2.3 Memory Topology & Process RSS Ceiling
77: Because the LG 32LR686BPSA possesses a total of 1.5 GB of system RAM, webOS enforces strict process resource budgeting:
78: - **Active Process RSS Budget**: **250 MB – 350 MB maximum Resident Set Size (RSS)** for `com.cinejoy.tv`.
79: - **Low Memory Killer (`lmkd`) Behavior**:
80:   - The webOS kernel utilizes cgroups and `lmkd` monitoring total system free pages.
81:   - If the application process exceeds ~350 MB RSS, or if overall system free memory drops below the low-water mark (~80–100 MB), the operating system issues an uncatchable **`SIGKILL` (`kill -9`)** to the WAM renderer process.
82:   - When SIGKILL occurs, no standard JavaScript unload handlers (`window.onbeforeunload`, `window.onunload`) are executed. The screen abruptly terminates, dropping the viewer back to the webOS Home Dashboard or the previous HDMI input with no crash message.
83: - **VRAM & Contiguous Memory Allocator (CMA)**:
84:   - Video hardware decoding surfaces (fMP4 frames) are allocated directly from kernel CMA buffers, separate from the Chromium V8 JavaScript heap.
85:   - However, uncompressed decoded image surfaces (such as TMDB backdrops and poster textures) are held in Chromium's GPU process memory. Loading too many full-resolution images simultaneously will trigger WAM process eviction.

89: ## 3. Step-by-Step LG Developer Mode Setup
90: 
91: To sideload and inspect applications on a physical LG 32LR686BPSA, the TV must be placed into **Developer Mode** using the official LG Electronics Developer Mode application.
92: 
93: ### 3.1 Prerequisites
94: 1. **LG Developer Account**:
95:    - Register a free developer account at: `https://webostv.developer.lge.com/`.
96:    - Ensure the account is verified via the confirmation email.
97: 2. **Network Connection**:
98:    - The TV and the development host PC must be connected to the **same local subnet** (e.g. `192.168.1.0/24`).
99:    - If using Wi-Fi, ensure router client isolation ("AP Isolation") is disabled so devices can communicate over port `9922`.
100: 
101: ### 3.2 Step 1: Install Developer Mode App on TV
102: 1. Power on the LG 32LR686BPSA TV.
103: 2. Press the **Home** button on the LG Remote to open the webOS launcher.
104: 3. Select **Apps** (LG Content Store).
105: 4. Click the **Search** icon (magnifying glass) at the top right.
106: 5. Type `Developer Mode` and search.
107: 6. Select the official **Developer Mode** app (published by LG Electronics Inc.).
108: 7. Click **Install**. Once installation completes, select **Launch**.
109: 
110: ### 3.3 Step 2: Sign In and Enable Dev Mode Status
111: 1. When the Developer Mode app opens, enter your LG Developer account credentials (Email and Password).
112: 2. Click **Sign In**.
113: 3. On the Developer Mode main dashboard, locate the **Dev Mode Status** toggle switch.
114: 4. Move the toggle from **OFF** to **ON**.
115: 5. A system prompt will appear:
116:    > *"TV needs to restart to change Developer Mode status. Do you want to restart?"*
117: 6. Select **Restart TV**.
118: 7. Wait for the TV to fully reboot back to the home screen.

121: 1. Re-open the **Developer Mode** app from the launcher bar.
122: 2. Confirm that **Dev Mode Status** is **ON**.
123: 3. Locate the **Key Server** toggle switch.

150: LG restricts developer sideloading to **50 continuous hours**:
151: - When the countdown reaches `00:00:00`, the Developer Mode daemon is disabled, the SSH daemon on port 9922 is terminated, and sideloaded IPKs are prevented from running.
152: - **Manual Renewal**: Open the Developer Mode app on the TV at any time and click the **EXTEND** button. This resets the timer back to 50:00:00.
153: - **Automated Renewal via CLI / Script**:
154:   Developers can maintain indefinite uptime by scheduling a periodic renewal request on their local workstation or home server using `curl` against LG's token renewal endpoint:
155:   ```bash
156:   curl -s -X GET "https://developer.lge.com/auth/login.dev?sessionToken=<TOKEN>"
157:   ```
158:   Or by triggering session extension via SSH / novacom:
159:   ```bash
160:   ares-novacom --run "echo 'extend' > /tmp/devmode_extend" -d lg1080p
